Michigan: what's on the November 3, 2026 ballot

Every candidate below is listed alphabetically, with party shown as text only. Open a name for their stated positions, background and recent news, each with sources.

Open Michigan on the map

Key dates

  • Last day to register online or by mail: October 19, 2026. From October 20 through Election Day you can still register in person at your city or township clerk's office if you bring proof of residency. Same-day registration closes at 8 p.m. on Election Day.
  • Statewide early in-person voting: October 24, 2026 to November 1, 2026. Every community must offer at least these nine days. Some communities may start as early as October 5. You can also vote in person with an absentee ballot at your clerk's office from September 24 until 4 p.m. on November 2.
  • Last day to request an absentee ballot by mail or online: October 30, 2026. Requests are due by 5 p.m. You can still request and fill out an absentee ballot in person at your clerk's office until 4 p.m. on November 2. Absentee ballots must arrive by 8 p.m. on Election Day, and postmarks do not count.
  • Election Day: November 3, 2026. Polls are open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.

Official election information: Michigan Department of State – Elections

Who's running

Only the U.S. Senate and governor races are loaded so far. Other statewide offices, ballot measures, U.S. House and local races aren't loaded yet. Check your sample ballot for the full list.

State

Governor / Lt. Governor

This is a four-year term and an open seat, because Governor Gretchen Whitmer cannot run again due to term limits. Governor and lieutenant governor are elected together on one ticket. The running mates are Winnie Brinks (with Benson), Jay DeBoyer (with James), Beau Parmenter (with Hudson), Robert Donald Cowper II (with Brandenburg) and Bobbie Clay (with Campbell).
